sanskrit: ūrdhvo bhava prati vidhyādhy asmad ugraṃ dhanur ojasvān ā tanuṣva | prati durhārdaṃ harasā śṛṇīhi kṛtvānam agne adharaṃ kṛṇuṣva ||
english: Rise up! Shoot back against them; O mighty one, draw your fierce bow with force. Strike down the ill-wisher with your blazing flame; O Agni, lay low the maker of sorcery.

sanskrit: praty enaṃ yāhi prati bhaṅdhy enaṃ vividhyann agne vitaraṃ vi bhāhi | pratyaṅ prehi vartmanā jarhṛṣāṇaḥ kṛtyākṛte duṣkṛte mādhi vocaḥ ||
english: Go back against him; shatter him! Piercing him, O Agni, blaze forth all the more. Advance in reverse along his very path, exulting; do not speak favorably upon the maker of sorcerous evil-deed.

sanskrit: yo no durhārd dhṛdayenābhivaste yaś cakṣuṣā manasā yaś ca vācā | pratyaṅ daṃṣṭrābhyām abhi taṃ bubhūṣan kṛtyākṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ nir dahāgne ||
english: He who assails us with ill-will in his heart — whether by the eye, by the mind, or by speech — turning back upon him with your fangs, desiring to overpower him, O Agni, burn out utterly the maker of sorcery, the evil-doer.

sanskrit: pratībodhaś caturakṣo divyo aśmeva vīḍubhit | prabhañjañ chatrūn prati yāhy agne kṛtyākṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ hṛdaye vidhya marmaṇi ||
english: O Counter-Watcher, four-eyed, heavenly one — like a stone that shatters the strong — go forth O Agni, crushing enemies; pierce the maker of sorcery, the evil-doer, in his heart, in his vital parts.

sanskrit: indra kṣatram abhi vāmam ojo 'jāyathā vṛṣabha carṣaṇīnām | apānudo janam amitrayantam uruṃ devebhyo akṛṇor ulokam ||
english: O Indra, you were born into sovereignty, into goodly might, O bull of humankind. Thrusting away the hostile man, you made wide space for the gods.

sanskrit: mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ parāvata ā jagāmā parasyāḥ | sṛkaṃ saṃśāya pavim indra tigmaṃ vi śatrūn tāḍhi vi mṛdho nudasva ||
english: Like a fearsome beast that roams crookedly and dwells on mountains, you have come from afar, from beyond. Sharpening your javelin, O Indra, your keen bolt — strike down the enemies, drive away the battles.

sanskrit: aṃhomuce pra bhare manīṣām ā sutrāmṇe sumatim āvṛṇānaḥ | idam indra prati havyaṃ gṛbhāya satyāḥ santu yajamānasya kāmāḥ ||
english: To the Deliverer from distress I bring forth my devotion, seeking good will from the Good Protector. Receive this oblation, O Indra; may the desires of the sacrificer come to fulfillment.

sanskrit: aṃhomucaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ yajñiyānāṃ virājantaṃ prathamam adhvarāṇām | apāṃ napātam aśvinau huve dhiya indriyeṇa na indriyaṃ dhattam ojaḥ ||
english: The Deliverer from distress, the bull of the sacrificial lords, the one who blazes foremost at rites — I call upon the Son of the Waters, the two Aśvins, through insight; endow us with heroic strength through your heroic power.

sanskrit: dhātāram indraṃ savitāram ūtaye huve devām̐ amṛtān martyaḥ san | śreṣṭhe no vasavo dhatta dhāmni mā radhāma dviṣate mo arātaye ||
english: Being mortal, I call upon Dhātṛ, upon Indra, upon Savitṛ for aid — the immortal gods. O Vasus, establish us in the highest domain; may we not fall prey to the enemy, nor to the malevolent one.

sanskrit: adhi bravītv adhivaktā na indro adhi bravītu savitā daivyena | svasti mitrāvaruṇā ca dhattāṃ rātriṃrātrim aharahaś ca devāḥ ||
english: Let our divine advocate Indra speak on our behalf; let Savitṛ speak with divine authority. May Mitra and Varuṇa grant welfare; and the gods, night after night and day after day.

sanskrit: adhi bravītu pṛthivī uta dyaur adhi bruvantu marutaḥ pṛśnimātaraḥ | yo no dveṣṭy araṇo yaḥ sanābhiḥ pavir iva nemer adharaḥ so astu ||
english: May Pṛthivī speak on our behalf, and Dyaus; may the Maruts, sons of Pṛśni, speak for us. He who hates us — whether a stranger or a kinsman — may he be brought low like the felloe of a wheel's nave.

sanskrit: yasya trayā gatam anuprayanti devā manuṣyāḥ paśavaś ca sarve | tan no devaṃ mano adhi bravītu sunīti no nayatu dviṣate mā radhāma ||
english: He whom the three — gods, men, and all cattle — follow in their going: may the divine mind speak on our behalf for him; may good guidance lead us; may we not fall prey to the enemy.
